title: Error displaying image that's in the characters folder. Mog Chrono Engine.

posts.author: nyapaka
posts.body:
Issue Summary —
I receive an error when trying to use the shield in the ABS Mode for the Chrono Engine by Mog.
Details —
It was working fine locally on my machine, and this error occurs on the HTML version uploaded to my website. This version is crucial to playtesting for my game, so I need it to work this way.
What tutorials or previous support threads have you referenced? —
I found some forum posts related to the same error, but the cause was different. I tried copying the file and naming it the same as the error. I am not a coder, and fear I would break things mucking around in the javascript files.
Are you using any plugins? —
It's the Chrono Engine Demo, so all of those Mog plugins for that.
Attach any illustrative screenshots,
full
event pages with no cropping, mock ups, etc. —
Done. Screenshot is the error. I have a file in that folder with that exact name now and it still displays that after several failed attempts to utilise the shield in the demo.
Engine can be found at:
https://mogplugins.wordpress.com/rpg-maker-mv/
My upload of it for testing:
https://maybe.masamunicorn.com/
Any and all help is greatly appreciated! ^,.^

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
The $ is usually not a problem and it can't be the folderpath either because there is no folderpath on the web version.
My guess for the reason would be the capitalisation in the filename.
On the internet, A.png and a.png are two different files, because A and a are two different letters.
On Windows there is a backfunction that loads the wrong file if the correct one does not exist, which makes Windows ignore capitalisation.
I suggest changing the image to all lower cases and upload the game again, then test again.

theoretically yes.
however if you try that it would be easier to edit the filename on the webserver as windows has its own opinion on when to handle mixed capitalisation correctly.
The problem is that solving the problem in windows means basically going all lowercase for all files, and since that would be real changes you'll need to edit the reference for that. And that will require a full uoload again.
only changing the filename to match the spelling on the server has to be done on the server, but if you have an FTP program for access that is actually a lot less work.
